data.title: Threatening debt collection letter (likely scam)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Cyprus) demands €287.40 by 6 August 2026 for an alleged phone-concluded prize-draw subscription, paid to a Lithuanian account of a private person. It has several scam hallmarks.
data.explanation: This letter demands €287.40 within 72 hours and threatens account seizure, a negative SCHUFA entry and criminal charges. It has typical scam or dubious-collector signs: extreme pressure, a foreign private account, vague fees and a claim that objecting is pointless. Do not pay yet. Check whether you ever had this subscription. If not, dispute the claim in writing and don't use the contact details in the letter. You can also get advice from a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) and report it to the police if it is fraud. A real seizure would need a court order first.

warnings: Payment is demanded within 72 hours to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual, a strong scam indicator.
The letter uses a generic salutation, threatens seizure, SCHUFA and criminal charges, and says objecting is pointless, which is typical pressure tactics.
The fees are unexplained and a collector cannot seize an account without a court order.
The claim is not itemised and names no contract date, so check whether the subscription ever existed.
